title: National Consultant to Assessment of IOM Livelihood/Community-Based Reintegration Interventions in East Hararghe, Ethiopia
description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency on migration. It works closely with governments, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners to promote humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all, providing services, technical assistance, and policy advice to both migrants and States. In Ethiopia, IOM supports the Government of Ethiopia (GoE) to reduce protection risks and respond to the needs of the most vulnerable populations. Its programming is guided by a rights-based approach that prioritizes safety, dignity, and accountability, while ensuring meaningful participation of affected individuals and communities. IOM is also committed to upholding child safeguarding principles and preventing sexual exploitation and abuse across all its interventions. Within this framework, the Protection Unit plays a central role in ensuring that the rights, safety, and dignity of migrants and displaced populations are upheld through a “do no harm” approach. It delivers both mainstreamed and specialized protection services, including child protection, prevention and response to gender-based violence, mental health and psychosocial support, counter-trafficking assistance, and support to vulnerable migrants through return and reintegration programmes. In addition, the unit strengthens national systems by building the capacity of government and partners, supporting policy development, enhancing referral mechanisms, and engaging communities to reduce protection risks and promote safer migration. East Hararghe is one of Ethiopia’s major migration-prone areas along the Eastern migration route, characterized by recurrent irregular migration, return migration, youth unemployment, limited livelihood opportunities, climate-related shocks, and socio-economic vulnerabilities. To address these challenges, the International Organization for Migration (IOM), in collaboration with government institutions, implementing partners, and local communities, has implemented a range of livelihood, community-based reintegration (CBR), and individual reintegration interventions aimed at improving economic self-reliance, strengthening community resilience, and promoting sustainable reintegration of returnees. These interventions have included the establishment and support of cooperatives, provision of livelihood assets and entrepreneurship and skills training, community infrastructure support, business development initiatives, and individual economic reintegration assistance across several woredas of East Hararghe. Over the years, these interventions have contributed to improved access to livelihood opportunities in target areas and enhanced community involvement in reintegration processes. However, recent monitoring findings, field observations, and stakeholder consultations indicate that several cooperatives and livelihood initiatives are facing challenges related to profitability, operational functionality, governance, member participation, access to finance, market linkages, and long-term sustainability after the completion of IOM interventions. In addition, infrastructure limitations such as inadequate access to electricity, water, transportation, and communication services continue to constrain the growth and competitiveness of some livelihood initiatives. Furthermore, under the upcoming interventions, IOM is keen to ensure local socio-economic contexts, livelihood systems, migration dynamics, and market opportunities, as well as the degree of coordination and integration among relevant IOM units and external stakeholders including the local government are taken into consideration during intervention design and implementation. Against this backdrop, the proposed assessment seeks to generate evidence on the livelihood and socio-economic context of East Hararghe, including existing livelihood zones, business opportunities, priority sectors, migration and re-migration dynamics, and community knowledge, attitudes, and practices that may influence reintegration outcomes. The assessment will examine the root causes of prior underperformance, assess the viability and sustainability of existing livelihood and cooperative models, identify feasible and scalable CBR business approaches for returnees and host communities, document lessons learned and good practices, and provide practical recommendations to strengthen future programming, sustainability strategies, and investment decisions aimed at achieving durable reintegration outcomes in East Hararghe. The consultant will be responsible to assess the socio-economic and livelihood context of East Hararghe and evaluate the performance, viability, sustainability, and effectiveness of community-based and individual reintegration interventions and identify factors that promote or hinder sustainable reintegrationto inform future livelihood programming and investment decision

Our more than 2,100 staff worldwide work as trusted advisors across diverse contexts, combining deep technical expertise, implementation techniques, and innovative technology to deliver locally informed, client-focused solutions that help organizations achieve measurable, sustainable impact. Palladium is part of GISI's global family of companies, which aims to create solutions for the world's most complex challenges. With annual revenues of $14 billion, GISI's approximately 15,000 employees are engaged in projects across 100 countries worldwide providing construction, program/project management, and engineering consulting services. Project Overview The GHSD America First Palladium Sole Source Award supports country-led efforts to strengthen health systems, advance global health security, and sustain essential health services in alignment with the America First Global Health Strategy. Leveraging Palladium's expertise in health systems strengthening, digital transformation, and data use, the project will strengthen governance, service delivery, and decision-making through integrated and interoperable systems across priority health programs. The award also supports stronger health financing, public financial management, and accountability mechanisms to promote resilient, efficient, and country-owned health systems. Duration and Funding This is a fixed-term, project-funded position with an initial term of 12 months (through September 2027). Employment is contingent upon the availability of funding, with the potential for extension based on project requirements and funding availability. Location This role is based in Palladium's Addis Ababa, Ethiopia office, with periodic travel within Ethiopia to project sites and regional offices. Applicants must have authorization to work in Ethiopia, as visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Position Summary The Health Insurance and Health Financing Specialist provides technical leadership and implementation support to strengthen Ethiopia's health insurance system and advance health financing reforms. Reporting to the Health Care Financing Technical Lead, the Specialist works day to day with the Ethiopian Health Insurance Service (EHIS), the Ministry of Health, and regional health bureaus to develop the national health insurance pooling roadmap, revise Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI) contribution schedules based on ability-to-pay evidence, strengthen indigent targeting and enrollment in pilot woredas, and define the content of the health insurance decision-support dashboards used by government leadership. Key Deliverables (Year 1) Technical content and stakeholder consultations for the national health insurance pooling roadmap, through to government endorsement. Revised CBHI contribution schedules and indigent-targeting criteria, applied in pilot woredas. Indicator definitions and business rules for the health insurance decision-support dashboard used by EHIS and Ministry of Health leadership. Enrollment, premium collection, and coverage analyses for pilot regions that feed the provider payment pilots. Verification-ready documentation for each insurance deliverable. Primary Responsibilities Support the design, implementation, and strengthening of Community-Based Health Insurance (CBHI), Social Health Insurance (SHI), and broader health financing reforms. Strengthen insurance coverage, enrollment, premium collection, and financial sustainability mechanisms, including revision of CBHI contribution schedules and indigent-targeting criteria based on ability-to-pay evidence. Support benefit package design and financial risk protection within CBHI and SHI schemes, in coordination with the Strategic Purchasing and Provider Payment Specialist. Lead consultations with EHIS, the Ministry of Health, regional health bureaus, and woreda CBHI schemes to build consensus on the pooling roadmap and secure its formal endorsement. Define the content, indicators, and business rules of the health insurance decision-support dashboard and support its adoption by EHIS and Ministry of Health leadership. Provide technical assistance and capacity strengthening to government institutions and key stakeholders. Facilitate stakeholder engagement, policy dialogue, and collaboration among government, development partners, and implementing organizations. Document and disseminate lessons learned, best practices, and project achievements.

description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. Ethiopia has one of the most complex human mobility environments in the world, with factors ranging from conflict, drought, environmental degradation, damage to basic services and infrastructure, to changing livelihood strategies in an evolving political and economic milieu where poverty, and progressive depletion of coping mechanisms available to the displaced and host communities exist in large portions of the country, often leading to more displacements. Health, Nutrition and MHPSS program in Ethiopia supports the vulnerable populations to cope with these situations by providing essential health and MHPSS services including medical consultations, nutrition, maternal and child health, health promotion and referrals to tertiary health facilities. The program has over 25 health facilities supported in Tigray, Amhara, South Ethiopia, Oromia, Dire Dawa, Benshangul Gumuz, and Somali regions working collaboratively with the Ethiopian Public Health Institute. These activities are integrated with MHPSS program to ensure wholistic approach to patient care. In addition, it supports the governments through health system strengthening activities. This is the position be required to support IOM Health and MHPSS Team towards the successful implementation of IOM Health, & MHPSS related projects in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. In addition, support the deputy director office at the EPHI. Under the overall supervision of the Programme Officer-Emergency Health and MHPSS, and the direct supervision Senior Project Associate, Health, Addis Ababa, the incumbent will be responsible for the supporting program activities in Addis Ababa. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration. title: Manager - Climate, Circular Economy & ESG (Consultant)
description: About Inkomoko Inkomoko supports entrepreneurs to grow their businesses in order to improve livelihoods, create jobs, and help communities thrive. In 2026, Inkomoko was listed by the Financial Times as the 5th fastest-growing company in Africa, supporting entrepreneurs across East and Central Africa to grow thriving businesses and build inclusive, resilient economies. Founded in 2012, Inkomoko has worked with more than 100,000 entrepreneurs, including thousands of refugee entrepreneurs. Inkomoko provides a combination of training, consulting, access to finance, and market-level systems change. We are the largest investor to refugee entrepreneurs in Africa. Inkomoko has 1000+ staff in 50 offices across Chad, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, and South Sudan. Through Inkomoko's 2030 strategic plan, we are adding 3 additional countries to serve more than 550,000 entrepreneurs and growing our $30M loan fund to impact 7M lives. INKOMOKO VALUES All staff at Inkomoko are connected to a shared set of organizational values: Purpose: be solutions-oriented, produce high-quality work, and be a global leader Achievement: push yourself to reach beyond what you previously thought possible. Improvement: be humble, engage in continuous growth through open & accurate feedback Bravery: willing to take risks, create a safe space for others, be compassionate, and inclusive We Eat Goat: we celebrate success and support each other in hard times. We do this work together in the spirit of turikumwe, tuko pamoja, abren nen, Kula na sawa, On est ensemble Inkomoko is an affirmative action/equal opportunity employer. Refugees, women, and persons who reflect the diverse communities we serve are strongly encouraged to apply. About The Opportunity & Responsibilities Inkomoko is strengthening its approach to climate resilience, circular economy, and sustainable enterprise development. We are seeking a senior consultant to lead an initial Circular Economy Pilot with local social sector organizations while helping build the institutional foundations for Inkomoko's longer-term climate and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) capability. The immediate focus will be on 15 high-potential refugee-led organizations (RLOs) in Kenya and Ethiopia, supporting them to identify, design, finance, and implement income-generating, climate-smart circular economy interventions focused on food security, renewable energy, and waste management. However, the mandate extends beyond successful delivery of the pilot. The consultant will develop the content, tools, processes, workflows, partnerships, and learning required to enable Inkomoko to integrate climate and environmental considerations more systematically into its enterprise-development model and evolving impact architecture. This is therefore a strategic, hands-on institution-building assignment. The successful candidate will need to move between strategy and execution: working directly with RLOs, building the capability of Inkomoko teams, developing practical tools and systems, engaging technical and financing partners, and translating learning from the pilot into institutional capabilities that can be applied beyond the initial project. This will be a 12 month Consultancy. Key Responsibilities Lead the Circular Economy Pilot Own the end-to-end delivery of the Circular Economy Pilot with 15 selected RLOs Design and facilitate an intervention-development process that enables RLOs to identify viable, climate-smart and income-generating opportunities Support RLOs to develop high-quality intervention proposals, including business models, implementation plans, financing requirements, risks, timelines, and expected outcomes Work closely with Investment and relevant Inkomoko teams to assess interventions and facilitate appropriate financing Provide technical oversight and coaching during implementation Ensure the 15 RLOs implement viable interventions and generate measurable economic, employment, environmental, and resilience outcomes Build Climate & Circular Economy Capability within Inkomoko Develop practical climate and circular economy content, tools, workflows, and guidance that can be embedded into Inkomoko's existing RLO and enterprise-development programming Develop and deliver a climate resilience module and train Inkomoko staff to deliver it effectively Build staff capability through training-of-trainers, field observation, coaching, and quality assurance Develop practical approaches for identifying climate-related opportunities and risks within enterprise and social-sector programming Create reusable tools and processes that enable country teams to integrate climate considerations without requiring specialist support for every intervention Lay the Foundations for Inkomoko's Climate & ESG Capability Work with BGS, MERL, Program Design & Innovation, Investment, and relevant leadership to identify how climate, environmental sustainability, and ESG considerations should progressively be integrated into Inkomo
